interactive.title: Order with negatives

explain.text:
When a sum mixes jobs, work out brackets first, then powers, then times and divide, and last add and take away. The order still applies when negatives are included,[^1] so in 1 + 2 × −3 the times goes first. 2 × −3 = −6, and 1 + (−6) = −5. Add and take away are equal partners, so you work them left to right, and times and divide are partners in the same way. BIDMAS lists A before S, but 8 − 3 + 2 is 5 + 2 = 7, not 8 − 5 = 3.

A power belongs only to the number it touches. In −3² the square touches the 3, so 3² = 9 comes first and the minus in front turns it to −9. To square the negative number itself, put it in brackets, so (−3)² = (−3) × (−3) = 9. A calculator needs those brackets to make the number negative and then square it,[^2] so it is best to use brackets whenever you square a negative.[^3] A minus in front of a bracket works on the whole bracket, so work the bracket out first. 10 − (3 − 5) = 10 − (−2) = 12, and −(5 − 8) is the opposite of −3, which is 3.

**Brackets, then powers, then times and divide, then add and take away, with partners left to right, and a power belongs only to the number it touches, so −3² = −9 while (−3)² = 9.**

practice.text:
**Rule of thumb:** Brackets, then powers, then times and divide, then add and take away. Partners go left to right, and a power touches only the number it sits on.

**Worked example:** 2 − 3 × (−2)². The bracket holds −2, and its square is (−2) × (−2) = 4. Times comes next, 3 × 4 = 12. Last, 2 − 12 = −10.

**Common mistakes**
- Squaring the minus in −3². The power belongs to the 3 alone, so −3² = −9. Only (−3)² = 9.
- Adding before taking away because BIDMAS lists A first. 8 − 3 + 2 goes left to right, 5 + 2 = 7, not 8 − 5 = 3.
- Dropping a bracket after a minus. 10 − (3 − 5) is 10 − (−2) = 12, not 10 − 3 − 5 = 2.
- Losing the sign of a cube. (−2)³ = (−2) × (−2) × (−2) has three minus signs, so it is −8, not 8.
